steps.title: Surveys — migration 9997_surveys_head_of_house.sql, RLS tests, domain and db wrappers
steps.goal: A second re-runnable migration `supabase/migrations/9997_surveys_head_of_house.sql` implements founder decision 8 on top of the survey schema already in `9999_init.sql`: the head of house (`household_role = 'head'`) with an account may answer `per_person` surveys for household members without accounts through a new client RPC `submit_survey_response_for(survey_id, person_id, answers)`, `list_survey_proxy_targets(survey_id)` tells a head whom they may answer for, `app.can_answer_for` and an extended `stamp_response_scope` (transaction-local `app.answer_for` setting) enforce the rule at the DB level, `survey_responses.answered_on_behalf` marks proxied rows, and the `survey_responses`/`survey_answers` update policies let the head edit those rows while the survey is open and `allow_edit`. A new RLS test file (`10_surveys_head_of_house.sql`) proves every positive and negative case, `09_grants.sql` includes the two RPCs, types are regenerated, and `@church/domain` (schemas, `validateSurveyAnswers`, status transitions, error keys) and `@church/db` (survey queries, RPC wrappers, query keys) are ready for the web (6.1b) and mobile (6.1c) steps. No UI; the founder gets a 'ready to paste' ledger row.

## Goal
When you finish, a second re-runnable migration `supabase/migrations/9997_surveys_head_of_house.sql` implements founder decision 8 — "the HEAD OF HOUSE (`household_role = 'head'`, or an adult designated head when there is no father) may answer `per_person` surveys on behalf of household members without accounts" — on top of the survey schema that `9999_init.sql` already holds: two new client RPCs (`submit_survey_response_for`, `list_survey_proxy_targets`), one helper (`app.can_answer_for`), an extended `stamp_response_scope` trigger, one extra column (`survey_responses.answered_on_behalf`), the adjusted `ca_survey_responses_*` / `ca_survey_answers_*` policies and grants. A new RLS test file proves the rule positively and negatively, `09_grants.sql` still passes with the two new RPCs in the client set, generated types are regenerated, and `@church/domain` / `@church/db` expose typed schemas, error keys, query helpers and query keys that 6.1b (web builder/results/CSV) and 6.1c (mobile responder) consume. No UI in this step. The founder gets a "ready to paste" ledger row in HANDOFF.md.

## Inputs / prior state
- `supabase/migrations/9999_init.sql` (steps 1.2–1.4c; frozen if the HANDOFF ledger shows it pasted): tables `surveys` (`title, description, audience_group_id not null, response_mode default 'per_person', allow_edit default true, status default 'draft', opens_at, closes_at, push default true, created_by`; check `closes_at > opens_at` when both set), `survey_questions` (`survey_id, org_id, position, kind question_kind, prompt, options jsonb, required`; `unique(survey_id, position)`, `unique(id, survey_id)`), `survey_responses` (`survey_id, org_id, person_id null, household_id null, submitted_by_user_id, scope_key not null, submitted_at, updated_at`; `unique(survey_id, scope_key)`), `survey_answers` (`response_id fk cascade, question_id, survey_id, org_id, value jsonb`; composite FK `(question_id, survey_id) → survey_questions(id, survey_id)`; `unique(response_id, question_id)`). Enums `survey_status (draft, open, closed)`, `response_mode (per_person, per_household)`, `question_kind (short_text, long_text, single_choice, multi_choice, yes_no, number, date)`. No `anonymous` column (Phase 4).
- Trigger functions from 1.3a: `app.freeze_survey_shape` (raises `survey_shape_frozen` P0001 once `status <> 'draft'`), `app.stamp_response_scope` (before insert/update on `survey_responses`: overwrites `person_id`/`household_id`/`scope_key`/`submitted_by_user_id` from the caller — `app.my_person_id(org)` — and raises `no_person_linked` when null), `app.on_content_publish` (enqueues a `notifications` row of kind `survey` when `status = 'open'` and `push`), `app.cancel_notifications_on_delete`. Read their real bodies in the file before touching them — the exact scope-key format (`person:<uuid>` / `household:<uuid>` or whatever 1.3a chose) must be preserved.
- RPC from 1.3b: `submit_survey_response(survey_id uuid, answers jsonb) returns uuid` — `require_user`; `survey_not_open`; `survey_not_in_audience` (`app.user_in_group(audience_group_id)`); `answers` is `{question_id: value}` with keys belonging to the survey else `invalid_payload`; unique violation → `survey_already_responded` unless `allow_edit` (then update + replace answers); `survey_edit_not_allowed`. Its error keys live in the section (5c) comment block; 1.3b explicitly deferred decision 8 to this step.
- Policies from 1.4a: `surveys`/`survey_questions` select = member ∧ open ∧ in window ∧ in audience, or `announcements.create`; insert `announcements.create`; update `announcements.edit`; delete `announcements.delete`. `survey_responses` select = own (`person_id = app.my_person_id(org)` or `household_id = any(app.my_household_ids())`) or the three announcement permissions; insert member ∧ writable ∧ open/in window/in audience; update own ∧ open ∧ `allow_edit` (per_household → any adult via `my_household_ids`); no delete. `survey_answers` via `exists` on the visible/own response. Read the exact policy names in the file (`ca_survey_responses_select`, `ca_survey_responses_insert`, `ca_survey_responses_update`, `ca_survey_answers_*` — whatever 1.4a named them).
- Helpers: `app.my_person_id(org)`, `app.my_household_ids()`, `app.user_in_group(group)`, `app.person_in_group(person, group)`, `app.can_edit_household(hh)`, `app.require_user()`, `app.require_writable(org)`, `app.has_perm`, `app.is_super_admin()`. Head of house = `persons.household_role = 'head'`, at most one per household (partial unique index from orchestrator decision 6; the designation UI is 5.1a/5.2b and, if adopted, the atomic `set_head_of_house` RPC of proposed step 5.8).
- Tests: `supabase/tests/helpers.sql` (`app_test.login(uid)`, `login_anon()`, `logout()`, `assert_count`, `assert_raises`, `assert_denied`), `supabase/tests/rls/01…09` — `06_events_surveys.sql` already covers open/closed/window/audience/shape-freeze/`survey_already_responded`/`no_person_linked`/per-household double response; `09_grants.sql` asserts the exact client RPC set via `has_function_privilege`. `scripts/db/{local-up,apply-migrations,check-rerunnable,test,gen-types}.sh`. If `supabase/migrations/9998_join_codes.sql` (5.6) exists, `apply-migrations.sh` applies files highest-number-first — confirm by reading it.
- Packages: `packages/domain/src/schemas/surveys.ts` (1.6b: `surveySchema`, `surveyQuestionSchema`, `surveyAnswersSchema`, `submitSurveyResponseSchema`), `packages/domain/src/errors.ts` (1.6b: `toDomainError`, the key catalogue), `packages/domain/src/permissions.ts` (`canManageSurveys`), `packages/db/src/rpc.ts` (1.7a: `submitSurveyResponse(db, { survey_id, answers })`), `packages/db/src/queries/surveys.ts` (3.6a created it with only the getter the dispatcher needs), `packages/db/src/keys.ts`, `packages/db/src/database.types.ts` (generated), `packages/db/src/type-tests/enum-parity.test-d.ts`.
- Ledger: `HANDOFF.md` "Applied migrations" says which files the founder has pasted. 9997 was reserved for surveys by 3.5b/3.6a/5.8; if the ledger shows 9997 taken, use the next free lower number and record it.

## Build
1. **Migration `supabase/migrations/9997_surveys_head_of_house.sql`**, following the skeleton in PLAN §4 / `docs/MIGRATIONS.md` and the per-construct rules (policies/triggers `drop … if exists` then `create`; columns `add column if not exists`; functions `create or replace`; every function `security definer set search_path = ''`; schema-qualified everything; policy names `ca_`; no `force row level security`; no enum value additions — none are needed). Header comment: purpose, founder decision 8 quoted, "re-runnable; paste after 9999_init.sql (and 9998 if present)", and the list of objects it (re)defines. Sections:
   - (0) the same owner `rolbypassrls` assertion as 9999.
   - (3) `alter table public.survey_responses add column if not exists answered_on_behalf boolean not null default false;` — true when the response was submitted by someone other than the person it is for; lets results, CSV and the mobile list say "answered by head of house" without joining `persons.user_id`.
   - (5) `create or replace function app.can_answer_for(target_person uuid) returns boolean` (stable, definer): true iff the caller has a person in the same org as the target (`app.my_person_id(target.org_id)`), that caller person has `household_role = 'head'` and `household_id = target.household_id`, and the target has `user_id is null`, `deceased_on is null`, `congregation_status in ('member','attendee')` and is not the caller. Super admins do not get a bypass here (answering surveys is a member act).
   - (5) `create or replace function app.stamp_response_scope()` — keep 1.3a's behaviour for the normal path byte-for-byte and add the proxy path: when `current_setting('app.answer_for', true)` is a non-empty uuid, require `app.can_answer_for(that uuid)` (else raise `survey_proxy_not_allowed` with errcode `42501` and a `detail` naming the reason: `not_head_of_house` / `different_household` / `person_has_account` / `person_not_active`), require the survey's `response_mode = 'per_person'` (else `survey_not_per_person`, `22023`), then stamp `person_id = target`, `household_id = target.household_id`, `scope_key` in the same format 1.3a uses for a person scope, `submitted_by_user_id = auth.uid()`, `answered_on_behalf = true`. On update, the proxy path applies only when the existing row's `person_id` equals the target. Without the setting, stamp `answered_on_behalf = false`. The setting is read with `current_setting(name, true)` and is only ever set transaction-locally (`set_config(…, …, true)`) by the RPC below; a direct table insert from PostgREST can never carry it, so client inserts stay self-only.
   - (5) `create or replace function public.submit_survey_response_for(survey_id uuid, person_id uuid, answers jsonb) returns uuid` (definer, `search_path = ''`): `perform app.require_user()`; load the survey (raise `survey_not_found`/`P0002` when missing — reuse an existing key if 1.3b has one); `app.require_writable(org_id)`; `app.can_answer_for(person_id)` else `survey_proxy_not_allowed` (42501); `response_mode = 'per_person'` else `survey_not_per_person` (22023); open + in window else `survey_not_open`; **the target person** in the audience via `app.person_in_group(person_id, audience_group_id)` else `survey_not_in_audience` (the head's own membership in the audience is irrelevant — a men's survey may be answered by a father for a son without an account); validate `answers` keys exactly as `submit_survey_response` does (factor the shared validation into `app.validate_survey_answers(survey_id, answers)` if 1.3b did not already, and have both RPCs call it — `create or replace` of `submit_survey_response` is allowed because the signature does not change); `perform set_config('app.answer_for', person_id::text, true)`; insert the response (the trigger stamps scope) mapping the `(survey_id, scope_key)` unique violation to `survey_already_responded` unless `allow_edit`, in which case update the existing row for that person and replace its answers (`survey_edit_not_allowed` when `allow_edit` is false); `perform set_config('app.answer_for', '', true)` in every exit path (use a nested block with `exception when others then … raise`); return the response id. Audit: if `app.audit_row` is trigger-only, do not add rows by hand — record in `docs/RLS.md` that proxy responses are identifiable by `answered_on_behalf` + `submitted_by_user_id`.
   - (5) `create or replace function public.list_survey_proxy_targets(survey_id uuid) returns jsonb` (definer): `require_user`; returns `[]` unless the caller's person is `head` of a household in the survey's org; otherwise a JSON array of `{ person_id, first_name, last_name, preferred_name, household_role, in_audience boolean, response_id uuid|null, submitted_at timestamptz|null }` for every household member for whom `app.can_answer_for(person_id)` is true, ordered by `household_role` then `last_name, first_name`. Reads `persons` directly inside the definer function (the caller cannot select `persons` columns — column grants — which is why this is an RPC and not a view); it exposes only names and role of the caller's own household, which the household already sees through `directory_persons`.
   - (7) `drop trigger if exists … ; create trigger` for `stamp_response_scope` on `survey_responses` only if 1.3a's trigger name must change — otherwise leave 9999's trigger in place (the function body was replaced in place).
   - (8) `drop policy if exists` + `create policy` for the `survey_responses` and `survey_answers` policies you must widen (re-create only those, with their 1.4a names): select — add the branch "the caller is head of a household and the response's `person_id` is a member of that household with `answered_on_behalf`" — in practice `household_id = any(app.my_household_ids())` from 1.4a already covers it; verify and keep as is if so; update — add `or (answered_on_behalf and app.can_answer_for(person_id))` alongside the existing own/adult branch, still ∧ survey open ∧ `allow_edit`; `survey_answers` select/insert/update mirror through the `exists` on the parent response. No delete policies. Every policy keeps the `app.org_writable` requirement on writes.
   - (9) `revoke execute on function public.submit_survey_response_for(uuid, uuid, jsonb), public.list_survey_proxy_targets(uuid), app.can_answer_for(uuid) from public;` then `grant execute … to authenticated` (and `app.can_answer_for` to `authenticated` because a policy calls it, like 1.4a did for the other `app.*` helpers referenced in policies). `service_role` gets nothing new.
   - Error catalogue: add to the comment block (or wherever 1.3b keeps the catalogue) `survey_proxy_not_allowed 42501`, `survey_not_per_person 22023`, plus `survey_not_found P0002` if new. Keep `raise … using errcode = …, message = '<key>', detail = '<reason>'` in the same style as 1.3b so `toDomainError` maps them.
2. **Apply and check locally** in the standing sequence; `apply-migrations.sh` twice must succeed with 9997 in place; `check-rerunnable.sh` must pass (it enforces the static rules on every migration file).
3. **RLS tests** — new file `supabase/tests/rls/10_surveys_head_of_house.sql` (same harness; `begin … rollback`): fixture = one org with a household of four persons — `head` with an account (`user_id` set, active membership), `spouse` with an account, `child` (age below `adult_min_age`, no account), `other` adult without an account — plus a second household whose `head` has an account, an `everyone` `per_person` open survey with two questions and a `men` survey; assert: head submits `submit_survey_response_for(survey, child, …)` → one `survey_responses` row with `person_id = child`, `household_id = the household`, `submitted_by_user_id = head`, `answered_on_behalf = true`, `scope_key` equal to what a self-submission for that person would produce; head sees that response and its answers (`assert_count`), spouse (same household) sees it too; the other household's head gets 0 rows; head for `spouse` (has an account) → `survey_proxy_not_allowed` with detail `person_has_account`; spouse (not head) for `child` → `survey_proxy_not_allowed` / `not_head_of_house`; other household's head for `child` → `different_household`; head for `child` on a `per_household` survey → `survey_not_per_person`; head for the `other` adult on the `men` survey when that person is female → `survey_not_in_audience`; second submission with `allow_edit = true` updates in place (still 1 row, answers replaced), with `allow_edit = false` → `survey_already_responded`; head updating the proxied row through a direct `update survey_responses` under RLS succeeds while open and `allow_edit`, fails (0 rows) after `closed`; a direct `insert into survey_responses` by the head with `person_id = child` is re-stamped to the head's own person (self path; the setting is absent), proving proxies only flow through the RPC; `list_survey_proxy_targets(survey)` as head → 2 entries (`child` with `response_id` set after the proxy, `other`), as spouse → `[]`, as the other household's head → its own household's members only; `anon` → 42501 on both RPCs; suspended org → `organization_suspended` from `submit_survey_response_for`. Update `09_grants.sql` so the intended client RPC set includes the two new functions and `authenticated` still cannot execute any `srv_*`. Extend `08_rerunnable.sql` only if it hard-codes object counts that 9997 changes (it should count after ALL migrations).
4. **Typegen**: `scripts/db/gen-types.sh` → `packages/db/src/database.types.ts` picks up the new column and the two RPCs; `enum-parity.test-d.ts` unchanged (no new enums).
5. **`@church/domain`**: `schemas/surveys.ts` — add `submitSurveyResponseForSchema` (`survey_id`, `person_id`, `answers: surveyAnswersSchema`), `surveyProxyTargetSchema` (the JSON shape above, `z.looseObject` like the other RPC results) and `surveyProxyTargetsSchema = z.array(...)`, `surveyResponseSchema` (row shape incl. `answered_on_behalf`), and a pure `validateSurveyAnswers(questions, answers)` → `{ ok: true } | { ok: false, errors: Record<question_id, string> }` enforcing `required`, `single_choice`/`multi_choice` values ∈ `options`, `yes_no` boolean, `number` finite, `date` `YYYY-MM-DD`, text length ≤ 2000 — the client-side mirror of what the RPC/DB accept (keep the DB as the authority; this exists so forms can show inline errors); `surveyStatusTransitions` = `{ draft: ['open'], open: ['closed'], closed: [] }` with `canTransitionSurvey(from, to)`. `errors.ts`: add `survey_proxy_not_allowed`, `survey_not_per_person`, `survey_not_found` with their SQLSTATEs and human messages (the proxy message uses the `detail` reason: "Only the head of house can answer for family members", "This person already has an account and answers for themselves", "This person is not in your household", "This person is not active in the directory"). Vitest cases for the validator (every kind, valid + invalid) and the transitions.
6. **`@church/db`**: `rpc.ts` — `submitSurveyResponseFor(db, { survey_id, person_id, answers })` → uuid, `listSurveyProxyTargets(db, { survey_id })` → parsed with `surveyProxyTargetsSchema`. `queries/surveys.ts` (extend 3.6a's getter additively): `listSurveys(db, orgId, { status? })` ordered `created_at desc`, `getSurvey(db, id)`, `listSurveyQuestions(db, surveyId)` ordered by `position`, `insertSurvey`, `updateSurvey`, `deleteSurvey`, `replaceSurveyQuestions(db, surveyId, questions[])` (delete-then-insert inside the draft state; the DB refuses after draft), `setSurveyStatus(db, id, status, { opens_at?, closes_at? })`, `listSurveyResponsesWithAnswers(db, surveyId)` (responses + nested answers; managers), `listOpenSurveysForMe(db, orgId)` (RLS does the audience/window filtering — a plain select ordered by `closes_at nulls last`), `getMyResponse(db, surveyId, { person_id?, household_id? })`, `countSurveyResponses`. `keys.ts`: `queryKeys.surveys.list(orgId)`, `.detail(id)`, `.questions(id)`, `.responses(id)`, `.myResponse(id, scopeId)`, `.proxyTargets(id)`. Unit tests with the mocked client pattern 1.7a uses.
7. **Docs**: `docs/RLS.md` — a "Surveys and head of house" subsection: the rule, the `app.answer_for` transaction setting, why proxies only flow through the RPC, the known consequence "if the head of house has no account but the spouse does, nobody can answer for the children until the household designates the account holder as head (5.1a/5.2b)", and the "Hidden household" consequence for survey managers who are not directory admins. `docs/MIGRATIONS.md` — add 9997 to the file list with its paste order. `supabase/README.md` — paste order now `9999 → (9998) → 9997`.

## Constraints

## Build

Questions editor `src/features/surveys/QuestionEditor.tsx`: `useFieldArray`, add question (kind select), move up/down (buttons — no drag library), remove, per-kind option editor; `position` = array index on save. When the survey is not `draft`, the form renders `response_mode`, `audience_group_id` and the entire questions editor **read-only** with the notice "Questions and audience are locked once a survey is open (answers already refer to them)"; only title, description, window, `allow_edit` and `push` remain editable — this mirrors `freeze_survey_shape`; if the DB still raises `survey_shape_frozen` map it to a form-level error.

Response table: one row per response — respondent (person "First Last" or household name; for `per_household` rows the household name; "Hidden household" when the directory view returns nothing because the manager is not a directory admin and the household is private — DESIGN §5's known consequence, state it in a footnote), `answered_on_behalf` → badge "answered by head of house", `submitted_at`, then one column per question (multi_choice joined with `; `, booleans Yes/No, dates `formatDateOnly`). 3. **Diff rendering** `src/features/audit/diff.ts`: `diffAuditRow(row): AuditChange[]` where `AuditChange = { key, label, before: string | null, after: string | null }` — for `UPDATE` only keys whose JSON differs between `old_data` and `new_data`; for `INSERT` every key of `new_data`; for `DELETE` every key of `old_data`; for the two synthetic actions whatever the RPC stored. ## Build

## Constraints
- The service client (`createServiceSupabase()`) appears ONLY in `src/lib/push/*`, `src/lib/cron/*`, `app/api/cron/tick/route.ts`, `src/features/announcements/push-actions.ts` (3.6a), `src/features/announcements/schedule-actions.ts` and `src/features/notifications/notification-actions.ts` (this step) — extend 3.6b's `git grep` whitelist in `docs/RLS.md` accordingly. Every service read/write is preceded by the user-client permission check and followed by an explicit `org_id` comparison; `srv*`/service helpers require the `ServiceDbClient` brand — never cast.
- The user-client update of `announcements.publish_at` happens BEFORE the service-side outbox move, never the other way round (if the user update fails, nothing moves). Never move `claimed`/`sent`/`failed`/`cancelled` rows; never set `scheduled_for` in the past through Reschedule (Publish now uses `now()`).
- No migrations (`9999_init.sql` may be frozen); no changes to `srv_claim_notifications`, the dispatcher's claiming logic, `refs.ts`, the cron phases, `proxy.ts`, `next.config.ts`, CSP, `apps/web/vercel.json`, or the mobile app. No raw `supabase.from(...)` in components, pages or actions — helpers go in `@church/db` additively with tests. No `persons`/`households` reads — recipient names come from `profiles` only.
- Do not build the audit pages (6.2a), account deletion (6.3) or anything mobile. Keep 3.5a/3.5b/5.3a/6.1b tables intact except the one-line `detailHref` pass-through and the notice text.
- Versions: Next 16.3, React 19.2.3 exact, supabase-js 2.112, Zod 4.5, TypeScript ~5.9 (not 7), ESLint 9 (not 10), Tailwind 4, Vitest 4, Playwright 1.62. No new runtime dependency except shadcn components generated into `src/components/ui/*` (`popover`, `alert-dialog` if absent).

Policies: select own, insert only via the RPC, update service role, no delete. `09_grants.sql` already proves `authenticated` cannot execute any `srv_*`. ## Build
1. **DB proof** — `supabase/tests/rls/11_account_deletion.sql` (same harness as `01…10`: `begin … rollback`, `app_test.login(uid)`, `assert_count`, `assert_raises`, `assert_denied`). Fixture: org A with two users — `mgr` (the only `users.edit_permissions` holder, linked person, one `push_devices` row, one `notification_preferences` row) and `member` (plain member, linked person); org B untouched. Assert: as `member`, `select request_account_deletion()` → one row in `account_deletion_requests` with `user_id = member`, `processed_at is null`; calling it again leaves one row (upsert, `requested_at` unchanged or refreshed — assert whatever the body does and say so in a comment); `member` selects exactly 1 row and `mgr` selects 0 of member's rows (own-only policy); `member` cannot `update`/`delete` the row (0 rows affected or 42501); `anon` → 42501 on the RPC; as `mgr`, `request_account_deletion()` then, as the service/owner role the harness uses for `srv_*`, `select srv_process_account_deletions()` → returns 2; afterwards `auth.users` has neither id, `persons.user_id` is null for both persons (the persons rows still exist), `org_memberships`/`org_membership_permissions`/`push_devices`/`notification_preferences` for both are gone, both requests have `processed_at not null`, and `audit_log` holds the "org has no manager" row for org A (the guard audited instead of blocking because of `app.cascade`); a second `srv_process_account_deletions()` returns 0. Add the test to `scripts/db/test.sh` only if it enumerates files by name (it should glob).
2. **Cron proof** — in `apps/web/src/lib/cron/tick.test.ts` (or the file 3.6b used) add a case that the final phase calls `srv_process_account_deletions` on the service client once per tick and reports its integer result in `phases[]`; if 3.6b already covers it, extend the assertion to the reported count and say so in HANDOFF. No change to the phase order.
3. **`@church/db`** — `packages/db/src/rpc.ts`: `requestAccountDeletion(db): Promise<void>` (add if missing). New `packages/db/src/queries/account.ts`: `getMyAccountDeletionRequest(db)` → the caller's row or null (RLS scopes it), exported from the package index; `keys.ts`: `queryKeys.account.deletionRequest()`. Unit test with the mocked client pattern of 1.7a.
4. **Web `/account` and `/account/delete`** — new route group `apps/web/app/(account)/`: `account/page.tsx` ("Your account": signed-in email from `getAuthContext()`, the list of churches from `my_context()` orgs with membership status, links to `/auth/reset` (change password), "Sign out" (existing Server Action) and "Delete account" → `/account/delete`) and `account/delete/page.tsx` — both call `requireUser('/account/…')`. Add `/account` to `proxy.ts`'s protected prefixes so anonymous requests redirect to `/login?next=%2Faccount%2Fdelete` (Google's reviewers open the URL logged out — the redirect to sign-in is expected). `src/features/account/DeleteAccountForm.tsx` (client) + `src/features/account/actions.ts` (`'use server'`): the page explains in plain words, generated from one shared copy module `src/features/account/deletion-copy.ts` (also mirrored in the mobile app, keep the strings identical): what deletion does — "Your sign-in, your devices and your church memberships are removed. The form requires typing `DELETE` (constant `DELETE_CONFIRMATION_WORD`) and a checkbox "I understand my church keeps the directory entry"; the Server Action `requestAccountDeletionAction()` re-checks the session with the user client, calls `requestAccountDeletion(db)`, maps errors with `toActionError`, then calls the existing `signOut` logic and redirects to `/account/deleted` (a static `(public)` page: "Your deletion request was received. 5. **Mobile "Delete account"** — screen `apps/mobile/app/account/delete.tsx` at the ROOT of `apps/mobile/app` (outside `(app)` so a signed-in person with no active church can reach it too — Play requires deletion for every user), guarded in the screen: no session → `router.replace('/(auth)/sign-in')`. Entry points: a "Delete account" row at the bottom of `app/(app)/(tabs)/more.tsx` in a "Danger" section under the existing privacy/terms links, and a small "Delete my account" text link on `app/(auth)/no-church.tsx` (below its explanation), both `router.push('/account/delete')`. Test `useRequestAccountDeletion` with injected deps (`rpc`, `signOut`, `navigate`) exactly like `registerForPush`'s tests: success order rpc → signOut → navigate; rpc failure → no signOut, error surfaced.
6. **`/privacy` and `/terms` real text** — `apps/web/src/content/legal.ts` exporting `LEGAL = { entityName: '<LEGAL_ENTITY_NAME>', contactEmail: '<FOUNDER_EMAIL>', postalAddress: '<POSTAL_ADDRESS>', governingLaw: '<STATE>', effectiveDate: '<YYYY-MM-DD>', domain: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL }` and `LEGAL_IS_DRAFT = true` (any `<…>` value still present also counts as draft), plus `privacySections` and `termsSections` (arrays of `{ id, heading, paragraphs: string[] }`) rendered by `src/features/legal/LegalPage.tsx` (h1, "Effective <date>", table of contents, a yellow "Draft for review — not yet published" banner while `LEGAL_IS_DRAFT`). Privacy policy sections, each stating only what the schema really stores (check `9999_init.sql` while writing): Who we are; What Anacast is (a church chooses to use it; the church, not the app, decides what goes into its directory); Account data (email, sign-in method — passwords and one-time codes are handled by our authentication provider, display name); Church directory data entered by your church or your household (names, address, phone, email, birthdate and its visibility setting, marital status, anniversary, household role, congregation status, photos, leader notes visible to church leaders only); Children (no child accounts — `save_person` refuses to link an account to a minor; children appear in the directory only as entered by a parent or the church, hidden from other congregations unless the family opts in via `show_children_in_fellowship`); Content (sermons, announcements, bulletins, documents, events, survey answers — survey answers are visible to church leaders and attributed to you or your household; the head of house may answer for family members without accounts); Notifications (Expo push token and platform per device, your per-church notification preferences; removed when you sign out or delete your account); Share links (visitor IP addresses are stored only as salted hashes for rate limiting); Audit log (leader actions such as permission and privacy changes are recorded for the church's own accountability); Who can see your data (congregation vs fellowship rule from DESIGN §5, leaders, super admin/operator); Service providers (Supabase — database, authentication, file storage, US East; Vercel — web hosting; Expo and Google Firebase Cloud Messaging — push delivery; Stripe — church billing, never members' cards; Resend — invitation emails when enabled; error reporting when enabled — "see the Monitoring section added in step 6.3b"); No advertising, no analytics, no sale of data; Your choices (privacy toggles `hide_from_fellowship`, `hide_from_congregation`, `show_children_in_fellowship`, per-field birthdate visibility, notification settings, account deletion at `<domain>/account/delete` with the exact list of what is deleted and what the church keeps — identical to `deletion-copy.ts`); Retention (cancelled churches purged after 30 days by `srv_housekeeping`; signed URLs expire within an hour; deletion requests processed automatically); Security summary (row-level security, private buckets, encrypted transport); Changes to this policy; Contact. Terms of service sections: Acceptance; The service and the church's role (church leaders are responsible for the data they enter and for their members' consent); Accounts and eligibility (adults only hold accounts); Acceptable use (no unlawful content, respect copyright of sermons/media you upload or link; external links are subject to the provider's terms); Subscription and billing (the church pays `<PRICE>` per month after a 30-day trial; the operator may suspend a church whose subscription lapses; no charges to members); Content ownership (the church and its members keep their content; the operator has the licence needed to run the service); Availability and changes; Termination (delete your account any time; the church may remove your membership); Disclaimer of warranties and limitation of liability (`<STATE>` law); Contact. Update the smoke test: `/privacy` and `/terms` still return 200 with one h1, contain the h2 "Your choices" and "Contact", and no longer contain the word "Placeholder".
7. **`docs/PLAY_DATA_SAFETY.md`** — the Play Console "Data safety" worksheet, filled in from the schema and this step: a table per Play category (Personal info: name, email, phone, address, other — birthdate, marital status, photos; Photos; Messages — none; App activity — survey responses, in-app content interactions none; App info and performance — crash logs "none until step 6.3b enables error reporting; then diagnostics, optional"; Device or other IDs — Expo push token/device id) with the columns Collected? / Shared? / Optional or required / Purpose(s) / Ephemeral? / Encrypted in transit (yes) / Deletion request mechanism (yes — URL). Then the form's direct questions with the answers: "Does your app collect or share any of the required user data types?" yes; "Is all of the user data collected by your app encrypted in transit?" yes; "Do you provide a way for users to request that their data is deleted?" yes — account deletion URL `https://<DOMAIN>/account/delete` (redirects to sign-in) and in-app path More → Delete account; "Data deletion: are there any other data deletion methods?" contact the church office / `<FOUNDER_EMAIL>` for directory entries; privacy policy URL `https://<DOMAIN>/privacy`; "Independent security review" no; target audience adults (13+ minimum age is not applicable — no child accounts); "Families policy" not enrolled; note that the app contains no ads, no analytics SDK (4.4). Add a "How this was derived" section pointing at the tables and a "Re-check when" list (Sentry enabled in 6.3b; any new table with personal data). Link it from `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md` and the README docs index.

Write the founder's to-do list into HANDOFF: fill `LEGAL` placeholders, set `LEGAL_IS_DRAFT = false`, decide `<PRICE>` wording, review both pages, then the Play Console needs the two URLs.

If the real `srv_process_account_deletions` body differs from DESIGN §4.4 in a way that makes the copy wrong, adjust the COPY to the truth and record the difference in HANDOFF "Deviations from plan"; do not "fix" the function here (that would be a `9996_*` migration and a founder paste — propose it instead).

## Goal
When you finish, both apps report unexpected errors to Sentry — but only when a DSN is configured, with no personal data in the events, and with zero change to builds and tests when the DSN is absent; the cron and push dispatcher tag their failures by phase so a broken tick is visible without reading Vercel logs; `docs/MONITORING.md` tells the founder how to create the Sentry projects, which env vars to set, what is and is not captured, and where to look (Vercel logs and Cron Jobs, Supabase reports, Expo build logs, the notification status pages from 6.2b) when something looks wrong; `scripts/db/security-audit.sh` runs the machine-checkable rows of `docs/CHECKLIST_SECURITY.md` against the local database and prints PASS/FAIL per row, CI runs it, and the checklist itself carries a dated run-through with results and evidence, plus a founder click-path for the rows only a dashboard can prove.

## Build
1. **Web Sentry SDK** — `pnpm --filter web add @sentry/nextjs` at the current major (check `npm view @sentry/nextjs peerDependencies` supports `next@16`; if it does not, stop, record it in HANDOFF, and implement only the DSN-less `captureException` shim below). Env (`src/lib/env.ts` + `apps/web/.env.example` + `docs/ENV.md`): `SENTRY_DSN` (server; optional), `NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN` (browser; optional — usually the same value), `SENTRY_ORG`, `SENTRY_PROJECT`, `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` (build-time source-map upload; optional; Vercel server env only), `SENTRY_ENVIRONMENT` (default `process.env.VERCEL_ENV ?? 'development'`). Files: `apps/web/sentry.server.config.ts`, `apps/web/sentry.edge.config.ts`, `apps/web/instrumentation-client.ts` (Next 16 convention) and `apps/web/instrumentation.ts` (`register()` imports the server/edge config by `process.env.NEXT_RUNTIME`; `export const onRequestError = Sentry.captureRequestError`). Every init is guarded: `if (!dsn) return;`. Options in all three: `dsn`, `environment`, `release: process.env.VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_SHA`, `sendDefaultPii: false`, `tracesSampleRate: 0.05` server / `0` client, no Replay, no profiling, `beforeSend` from `src/lib/monitoring/scrub.ts` (pure, unit-tested): delete `event.user.email`/`ip_address`/`username`, delete `request.cookies`, drop `authorization`/`cookie`/`x-cron-secret` headers, redact email-shaped strings and `sb_secret_…`/`sb_publishable_…`/`eyJ…` tokens in `message`, `exception.values[].value` and breadcrumb messages with a fixed regex set; keep `user.id` (a uuid) and tags. `next.config.ts`: wrap with `withSentryConfig(config, { org, project, authToken, silent: true, widenClientFileUpload: true, disableLogger: true })` only when `SENTRY_DSN || NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN` is set; otherwise export the plain config so the mock-env build is byte-for-byte the same as before. CSP: extend 2.1a's builder so `connect-src` also lists the DSN's origin (parse `new URL(dsn).origin`) when `NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN` is set — unit test both branches; do not add `unsafe-*`, do not use the tunnel route (it would widen the matcher in `proxy.ts`).
2. **Web capture points** — `src/lib/monitoring/index.ts`: `isMonitoringEnabled()`, `captureException(err, { tags?, extra? })` (no-op without DSN; never throws), `withMonitoring(name, fn)` wrapper. Use it in exactly these places, additively: `runTick`'s `phase()` — on failure `captureException(error, { tags: { area: 'cron', phase: name } })`; `dispatchQueued`/`processReceipts` — per-notification failures that are not `DeviceNotRegistered` (tag `area: 'push'`); `app/api/stripe/webhook/route.ts` — the 500 path (tag `area: 'stripe'`, extra `eventType`, never the payload); `toActionError` — only when the error is NOT a mapped domain error (SQLSTATE known to `errors.ts`) and not a Next redirect/notFound (`isRedirectError`), tag `area: 'action'`; `app/global-error.tsx` and `app/(org)/o/[orgSlug]/error.tsx`-style boundaries → `Sentry.captureException` in a `useEffect` (create `app/global-error.tsx` if 2.1a did not). Set `Sentry.setUser({ id })` in `getAuthContext()` when enabled — id only.
3. **Mobile Sentry SDK** — from `apps/mobile`: `npx expo install @sentry/react-native` (version from `expo install` only). `src/lib/monitoring.ts`: `initMonitoring()` — reads `EXPO_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN` through `publicEnv()` (add it as optional), returns without side effects when empty; otherwise `Sentry.init({ dsn, environment: Updates.channel ?? 'development' (or `__DEV__ ? 'development' : 'production'` if expo-updates is not installed — do not install it), release from `expo-constants` version, sendDefaultPii: false, enableNativeCrashHandling: true, tracesSampleRate: 0, beforeSend: scrub })`; the scrub is a copy of the web regex set in `src/lib/monitoring-scrub.ts` (pure, unit-tested; do not import web code); `captureException(err, ctx)` and `setMonitoringUser(id | null)` helpers. Call `initMonitoring()` at the top of `app/_layout.tsx` before providers, wrap the root layout with `Sentry.wrap` only when enabled (export `Sentry.wrap(Root)` vs `Root` through a tiny `withMonitoring(Component)` so the disabled path has no Sentry reference at runtime), call `setMonitoringUser(session?.user.id ?? null)` from `SessionProvider` on session change, and clear it in `signOutEverywhere()` via the existing `registerBeforeSignOut` hook. `app.config.ts`: add the plugin `['@sentry/react-native/expo', { organization: process.env.SENTRY_ORG, project: process.env.SENTRY_PROJECT }]` ONLY when `SENTRY_ORG && SENTRY_PROJECT && SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` are all present (source maps upload during EAS builds), so `expo-doctor`/`expo export` without them are unchanged; document the three as EAS secrets in `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md`. Add `app/+error.tsx`? No — expo-router has no such file; instead wrap the `(app)/_layout` tree in a small `ErrorBoundary` component (`src/components/ErrorBoundary.tsx`, class component, "Something went wrong — Reload" button that resets state) which calls `captureException`. `docs/PLAY_DATA_SAFETY.md`: update the "App info and performance → Crash logs / Diagnostics" row to "collected when the church operator enables error reporting; not linked to identity beyond an internal user id; not shared for advertising" and the privacy page's Service providers paragraph (`legal.ts`) to name "an error-reporting service (Sentry) when enabled".
4. **`docs/MONITORING.md`** — sections: What is monitored (the capture points above, the tags `area`/`phase`, what is scrubbed, what is never sent — emails, tokens, cookies, request bodies, directory data); Turning it on (founder click-path: sentry.io → Create project → platform Next.js → copy DSN → Vercel → Settings → Environment Variables → `SENTRY_DSN`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN` (Production + Preview), `SENTRY_ORG`, `SENTRY_PROJECT`, `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` (server only) → redeploy; second project platform React Native → `EXPO_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN` as an EAS environment variable plus the three build secrets → next `eas build`); Alerts (Sentry → Alerts → "issues" rule: new issue in `cron` or `stripe` area → email `<FOUNDER_EMAIL>` — placeholder); Where to look when something is wrong (Vercel → Deployments → Functions logs; Vercel → Settings → Cron Jobs → last runs and the JSON phase report; Supabase → Reports and Logs → Postgres/Auth; Supabase Free plan pause after 7 idle days → Restore; Expo → Builds; the org `/o/<slug>/notifications` page (6.2b) for stuck `queued` pushes; `/admin/audit` (6.2a)); Manual health check (`curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $CRON_SECRET" https://<VERCEL_URL>/api/cron/tick | jq '.ok, [.phases[] | {name, ok, ms}]'` — expected every `ok: true`); Cost/plan notes (Sentry free tier limits; sampling values above). Link it from README's docs index and from `docs/DEPLOY.md`.
5. **Security audit script** — `supabase/tests/security/audit.sql` + `scripts/db/security-audit.sh` (runs it with `psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 "$DATABASE_URL"`; prints one line per check `PASS|FAIL <id> <description> [<offenders>]` using `do $$ … raise notice` blocks or a temp table + final `select`; exits non-zero when any FAIL). Checks (ids stable so the checklist can cite them): `SEC-01` every table in `public` has `relrowsecurity = true` and none has `relforcerowsecurity`; `SEC-02` every policy on `public.*`/`storage.objects` is named `ca_%`; `SEC-03` `anon` has no `execute` on any function in `public` and `app` (`has_function_privilege('anon', oid, 'execute')`) and no table privileges beyond what `09_grants.sql` allows (list the exceptions 1.4b documented, e.g. none); `SEC-04` `authenticated` has no `execute` on `public.srv_%`; `SEC-05` every function in `public` and `app` is `prosecdef` and its `proconfig` contains `search_path=`; `SEC-06` no function body in `public`/`app` references unqualified `crypt(`/`gen_salt(`/`gen_random_bytes(`/`digest(` (regex on `prosrc`); `SEC-07` every row in `storage.buckets` has `public = false` and the `sermon-media` `file_size_limit` ≤ 52428800 while HANDOFF says Free (print the value); `SEC-08` `storage.objects` has no `update`/`delete` policy whose roles include `authenticated`; `SEC-09` column-level: `authenticated` lacks `select` on `persons.birthdate`, `persons.user_id` (read the exact revoked column list from 1.4b/`docs/RLS.md`) and on `households.hide_from_*` if 1.4b revoked them; `SEC-10` `private` schema: no privileges for `anon`/`authenticated`/`service_role` on `private.*`; `SEC-11` `audit_log` has no insert/update/delete policy for `authenticated`; `SEC-12` `account_deletion_requests` has no delete policy. Wire `scripts/db/security-audit.sh` into `.github/workflows/ci.yml` after `test.sh` (same non-blocking mode 1.1 chose, or blocking if 3.7a made the DB job blocking — match it) and into `docs/MIGRATIONS.md`'s verification sequence.
6. **Checklist run-through** — rewrite `docs/CHECKLIST_SECURITY.md` so each row has: item, why, how to check (command with `SEC-nn` or dashboard click-path), expected, and a new "Run-through <date> (local)" column filled by actually running everything you can now: the audit script rows, `scripts/db/test.sh` (grant matrix), the smoke suite (`noindex`/no-referrer on `/s/*`, CSP + HSTS on `/privacy`, no secret in HTML), `grep -rn "SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY" apps/web/src apps/mobile/src` → only `src/lib/env.ts`/`service.ts` on the web and nothing in mobile, `grep -rn "createServiceSupabase\|service.ts" apps/web/app apps/web/src` → only Route Handlers/Server Actions listed by name (share unlock, cron, webhook, createUserDirect, 6.2b's reschedule/deliveries actions, push dispatch) — list every hit and mark any unexpected one as a finding to fix in this step. Rows only a hosted dashboard can prove (secret key only in Vercel server env, custom SMTP configured, Stripe webhook secret set and signature verified with a test event, buckets private on the hosted project, OTP template, Site URL/redirect list, Supabase "Enforce SSL", Vercel deployment protection off for `/api/stripe/webhook` and `/api/cron/tick`) go into a "Founder run-through" section with a click-path each and an empty "date / result" column plus the one-line `helper` command where one exists (e.g. `curl -sI https://<VERCEL_URL>/s/unknown | grep -i x-robots-tag`). Add the two new rows "error reporting scrubs PII (unit test `scrub.test.ts`)" and "error reporting is off without a DSN (build/export unchanged)". Record every FAIL you found and fixed in HANDOFF "Deviations from plan" and in the row itself.
7. **Tests** — web: `scrub.test.ts` (emails, `sb_secret_`, JWT-looking strings, cookies/headers removed; uuids and tags kept), `csp.test.ts` extension (with/without DSN), `monitoring.test.ts` (no DSN → `captureException` no-op and `isMonitoringEnabled() === false`; with DSN → `Sentry.captureException` called with tags — mock `@sentry/nextjs`), cron test extension (a throwing phase is reported with `{ area: 'cron', phase }`); mobile: `monitoring-scrub.test.ts`, `monitoring.test.ts` (init skipped without DSN; `withMonitoring` returns the component untouched), `ErrorBoundary.test.tsx` if the mobile Vitest setup renders components (else a pure test of its `getDerivedStateFromError`/reset logic). Playwright smoke: with the mock env (no DSN) the HTML of `/`, `/login`, `/privacy` contains no `sentry` script or `ingest.sentry.io` reference and the CSP `connect-src` has no Sentry origin; add a second smoke config case only if 3.7a's harness supports per-test env — otherwise assert the CSP branch in the unit test only and say so.

## Constraints
- Error reporting is opt-in by env: with no DSN the web build output, the CSP, the mobile export and every test must be identical to before. Never enable Sentry in Playwright or CI mock env. No Session Replay, no profiling, no performance tracing on the client, no `sendDefaultPii`. Never capture domain errors (`errors.ts` keys), redirects, or 4xx auth failures — those are expected behaviour.
- No analytics or tracking SDK (4.4). No `tunnelRoute`. `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` is server/build-only and never `NEXT_PUBLIC_`/`EXPO_PUBLIC_`. No secret, DSN, email or model identifier in code, docs or tests — placeholders (`<FOUNDER_EMAIL>`, `<VERCEL_URL>`, `<DOMAIN>`).
- Web: `pnpm add` for `@sentry/nextjs` only (check the Next 16 peer range first); mobile: `npx expo install @sentry/react-native` only, run from `apps/mobile`; `react` stays 19.2.3 exact via the catalog. No migration; the audit script only reads catalogs. Do not edit `9999_init.sql`. If an audit check FAILS because of a real grant/policy bug, fix it with the next free descending migration named in the HANDOFF ledger (re-runnable per `docs/MIGRATIONS.md`) and record it — do not silently relax the check.
- Do not restructure `next.config.ts`, `proxy.ts`, `app/_layout.tsx` beyond the guarded additions above.

- `pnpm turbo lint typecheck test` → green (new scrub/monitoring/CSP/cron/mobile tests); `pnpm --filter web build` with the mock env (no DSN) → same route list as 6.3a and no Sentry webpack output; `NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN=https://examplePublicKey@o0.ingest.sentry.io/0 SENTRY_DSN=$NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN pnpm --filter web build` → succeeds (source-map upload skipped without `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN`, no error) and `curl -sI` of `/privacy` on `pnpm --filter web start` shows `connect-src` containing `https://o0.ingest.sentry.io`.
- `pnpm --filter web test:e2e:smoke` → green (no-Sentry assertions).
- `pnpm --filter mobile exec expo-doctor` and `npx expo export --platform android` (no DSN, no `SENTRY_*`) → clean; `grep -n "sentry" apps/mobile/app.config.ts` → the plugin is inside the `if (SENTRY_ORG && SENTRY_PROJECT && SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN)` branch.
- `grep -c "PASS\|FAIL" docs/CHECKLIST_SECURITY.md` → ≥ 12 (the run-through column is filled); `grep -n "SEC-0[1-9]\|SEC-1[0-2]" docs/CHECKLIST_SECURITY.md supabase/tests/security/audit.sql` → every id in both.
- Manual (optional, needs a throwaway Sentry project): set the DSN locally, throw inside a Server Action, confirm the event arrives with `user.id` only and no cookies.
